context_text: Export Development Canada is Canada's export credit agency and a federally owned Crown corporation supporting trade. It supplies financing and insurance and other export risk/market support to Canadian international businesses.
question: Quel rôle joue Exportation et développement Canada pour les entreprises qui font du commerce international?
reference_answer: Exportation et développement Canada (EDC) est l'organisme canadien de crédit à l'exportation et une société d'État fédérale. Il aide les entreprises canadiennes à développer leurs activités sur les marchés internationaux, notamment en offrant des solutions de financement, d'assurance-crédit, de garanties et de gestion des risques liés au commerce extérieur.

2017-11-02

context_text: Parks Canada explicitly says campsite reservation fees do not necessarily include national park entrance fees. Visitors need valid admission when entry fees apply; free-admission windows such as summer 2026 don't turn a reservation into an admission pass.
question: When reserving a campsite with Parks Canada, does the reservation automatically give me a national park admission pass?
reference_answer: No. A Parks Canada campsite reservation is separate from park admission. If admission fees apply, you must obtain an applicable park admission pass or pay the required daily admission in addition to reservation/camping fees, unless a particular fee exemption applies. A Discovery Pass is one option for admission, not automatically provided with the booking.
gc_llm_answer:
No, when you book a campsite, you pay only for the campsite and the admission pass is not included. You will need to pay for the admission pass at the park's entrance, or at the campground office, if it is open. How do I know which national parks are open to visitors? The Parks Canada website lists all national parks and their current status. You can also call the park directly to ask if it is open to visitors. What are some of the activities that are not allowed in national parks? Some activities that are not allowed in national parks include:

- Camping outside of designated campsites

- Building fires outside of designated fire pits

- Hunting and fishing (unless specifically allowed by the park)

- Removing plants or animals from the park

- Vandalizing park property

- Littering

- Driving off-road vehicles

- Engaging in other activities that may harm the park's environment or wildlife.

context_text: Federal reprisal complaint ordinary time limit is 60 days from known/ought-to-have-known date. Commissioner may grant extension depending on circumstances; policy revised October 8 2026.
question: Dans le régime fédéral de protection des divulgateurs, à partir de quand calcule-t-on le délai pour porter plainte pour représailles?
reference_answer: Le délai ordinaire pour déposer une plainte de représailles auprès du Commissariat à l'intégrité du secteur public du Canada est de 60 jours à partir du jour où la personne savait, ou aurait dû savoir, qu'une mesure de représailles avait été prise. Le commissaire peut proroger ce délai selon les circonstances. La politique du 8 octobre 2026 précise que le simple fait de découvrir tardivement la loi ne suffit pas nécessairement à justifier une prolongation.
gc_llm_answer:
La période commence à la date à laquelle la personne a pris connaissance des représailles ou aurait dû en avoir connaissance, ou à la date à laquelle la personne a pris connaissance de l’existence du régime fédéral de protection des divulgateurs, la plus tardive de ces deux dates étant retenue.

Il y a des différences dans les définitions, la portée et la procédure, ainsi que dans la manière dont les divulgateurs sont protégés. Les divulgateurs devraient consulter les lois et les règlements provinciaux et fédéraux pour comprendre les différences entre les régimes de protection des divulgateurs.

Le régime de protection des divulgateurs est-il le même pour tous les secteurs?Non. Le régime de protection des divulgateurs n’est pas le même pour tous les secteurs. Il existe des différences dans les définitions, la portée et la procédure, ainsi que dans la manière dont les divulgateurs sont protégés, selon le secteur. Les divulgateurs devraient consulter les lois et les règlements provinciaux et fédéraux pour comprendre les différences entre les régimes de protection des divulgateurs dans leur secteur spécifique.

question: Si je retire de l’argent de mon CELI pendant que je suis non-résident, puis-je recotiser en franchise d’impôt sans redevenir résident?
reference_answer: Non. Un non-résident du Canada peut retirer de l'argent de son CELI sans impôt canadien sur le retrait, et ce retrait crée normalement des droits de cotisation à compter du 1er janvier suivant. Cependant, une cotisation effectuée alors que la personne est non-résidente est imposable, généralement à 1 % par mois tant qu'elle demeure dans le compte, même s'il existe des droits inutilisés. Vous devez avoir été un résident du Canada pendant au moins 365 jours au cours des cinq années précédant l’année de la cotisation.

Vous devez avoir été un résident du Canada pendant au moins 365 jours au cours des cinq années précédant l’année où vous avez demandé la déduction. context_text: NWT property assessment assigns land/building value and is distinct from the property-tax notice. NWT taxes generally use assessed value × mill rate / 1000; municipal tax communities and general taxation areas have different taxing authorities.
question: What is the difference between a property assessment and a property tax bill in the Northwest Territories?
reference_answer: A property assessment in the Northwest Territories assigns a taxable value to a property; it is not the bill itself. The relevant taxing authority applies a tax rate or mill rate and applicable adjustments to the assessed value to determine the taxes owed. NWT Municipal and Community Affairs handles assessments, while municipal or territorial authorities administer taxation depending on location.
gc_llm_answer:
Property assessment is the process of placing a dollar value on a property for taxation purposes. You will receive a notice of assessment, which shows the assessed value of your property. Your property tax bill is calculated by multiplying the assessed value by the tax rate that applies to your property.

The assessed value of your property is used to determine how much you will pay in property tax. If you disagree with the assessed value of your property, you can file an appeal with the Northwest Territories Assessment Appeal Board.

Property tax bills are issued annually, usually in July or August. The amount of property tax you pay is determined by the assessed value of your property and the tax rate that applies to your property. The tax rate is set by the Government of the Northwest Territories and is applied to the assessed value of your property to determine the amount of property tax you will pay.

context_text: Under s9(1)(a), a renouncing Canadian must already possess another country's citizenship or become one upon acceptance. Humanitarian ministerial discretion in s9(2) waives only s9(1)(d) or (e); it cannot waive other nationality requirement (a).
question: Puis-je renoncer à ma citoyenneté canadienne si cela me rend apatride?
reference_answer: Non, pas selon la procédure ordinaire de renonciation prévue à l'article 9 de la Loi sur la citoyenneté. Vous devez déjà posséder une autre nationalité ou l'acquérir si votre demande est acceptée, afin de ne pas devenir apatride par cette renonciation. Le ministre peut dispenser de certaines autres conditions pour motifs d'ordre humanitaire, mais cette dispense ne s'étend pas à l'exigence d'une autre nationalité.
gc_llm_answer:
Oui. Vous devez demander la permission du ministre de la Citoyenneté et de l’Immigration. Le ministre peut vous accorder la permission de renoncer à votre citoyenneté canadienne si vous êtes apatride. Si vous renoncez à votre citoyenneté canadienne, vous n’êtes plus citoyen canadien. Cela signifie que vous ne pouvez plus vivre au Canada, voter, présenter une demande de passeport canadien ni bénéficier de l’aide consulaire du Canada à l’étranger. Si vous avez des enfants à l’étranger, ils peuvent ne pas être admissibles à la citoyenneté canadienne par filiation, même s’ils sont nés de parents canadiens. Vous pourriez être considéré comme un étranger, ce qui peut entraîner l’obligation de détenir un visa pour entrer au Canada ou dans les pays d’Europe qui font partie de l’Espace Schengen. Vous pourriez également être tenu de payer l’impôt sur le revenu au Canada, même si vous ne vivez pas au Canada. Si vous avez la double citoyenneté, vous conservez votre autre citoyenneté même si vous renoncez à votre citoyenneté canadienne. L’apatridie n’est pas définie de la même façon dans toutes les lois. Si vous êtes né d’un père qui est citoyen d’un autre pays, vous pourriez ne pas être considéré comme apatride si vous ne demandez pas la citoyenneté de son pays. Vous devriez obtenir des conseils juridiques avant de décider de renoncer à votre citoyenneté canadienne. Pour en savoir plus sur la renonciation à la citoyenneté canadienne, consultez le site Web de Citoyenneté et Immigration Canada. Si vous avez besoin d’aide juridique, vous pouvez communiquer avec le service Assistance juridique générale. Ce service offre de l’information, des conseils et des références à des avocats et à des parajuristes autorisés en Ontario, ainsi que des renseignements sur le système juridique en Ontario. Vous pouvez communiquer avec le service par téléphone, par courriel ou en ligne. Il n’y a pas de frais pour utiliser le service et vous n’avez pas besoin d’être un citoyen canadien pour y avoir accès. Si vous êtes dans un refuge, vous pouvez aussi appeler la ligne d’aide aux victimes de mauvais traitements. La ligne d’aide est accessible 24 heures sur 24, sept jours sur sept, partout en Ontario. Elle est également accessible depuis les refuges pour femmes violentées. Les services sont offerts en plusieurs langues. Si vous êtes en danger immédiat, composez le 911 ou le numéro de téléphone local de la police. Si vous avez besoin d’une aide immédiate, vous pouvez également vous adresser à l’organisme de services sociaux de votre collectivité ou au bureau de la bande. Le personnel vous aidera à trouver un endroit sûr où vous pourrez vivre.

context_text: Ontario IPC hears appeals of municipal and provincial access-to-information decisions, including refusal or fee disputes. For requests after July 1 2026 Ontario institutions generally have 45 business days, and appeal deadlines use 30 business days; earlier requests follow old regime.
question: Who hears an appeal if an Ontario municipality refuses my request for municipal records?
reference_answer: The Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario (IPC) independently handles appeals from access decisions made by municipalities and other bodies covered by the Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act. Check the decision letter for appeal instructions and deadline; the IPC first reviews jurisdiction and may use mediation or adjudication.
gc_llm_answer: You may appeal to the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario if you are refused access to municipal records. You should send the appeal to the Commissioner’s office within 30 days of the date of the refusal. The Commissioner’s office will send a copy of the appeal to the municipality. You may also appeal to the Ontario Division of the Court of Appeal if you are refused access to municipal records. You should send the appeal to the Court’s office within 30 days of the date of the refusal. The Court’s office will send a copy of the appeal to the municipality.

context_text: When both French and English chosen by federal-court parties, judge or other hearing officer must understand both without interpreter. The bilingual-competence duty applies to adjudicative functions and is not equivalent to banning all court interpretation services.
question: If both official languages are chosen by the parties in a federal court proceeding, can the judge rely on an interpreter to understand one of them?
reference_answer: No, not for understanding the evidence and arguments in the chosen official languages. Under section 16(1)(c) of the federal Official Languages Act, if the parties choose both English and French in proceedings before a federal court, the court must ensure that every judge or other officer hearing the case understands both languages without an interpreter. The requirement concerns the court's adjudicative functions, not every employee or every courtroom service.
gc_llm_answer: No. You must be able to hear and understand both official languages if both are chosen by the parties in a federal court proceeding. You must also be able to understand any language other than English or French that is chosen by the parties in a federal court proceeding. 9. Do judges have to live in the judicial district where they work? Yes. A judge must live in the judicial district where he or she works, unless otherwise authorized by the Commissioner for Federal Judicial Affairs. 10. Do judges have to continue to educate themselves about the law and other matters? Yes. Judges must commit to life-long learning. This includes regularly updating their knowledge of the law by reading decisions of other courts, articles and books. Judges also participate in formal judicial education programs. 11. What kind of training do judges get? All newly appointed judges participate in the National Judicial Institute’s orientation program for newly appointed judges. Judges also participate in other judicial education programs throughout their careers. These programs are delivered by the National Judicial Institute. The National Judicial Institute is an independent, non-profit institution dedicated to helping judges enhance their performance as judges and thereby improve the quality of the judicial system in Canada. 12. It reports its findings to the Canadian Judicial Council. The Canadian Judicial Council has the power to review the fitness for office of federally appointed judges. The Canadian Judicial Council makes recommendations to the Minister of Justice about whether a judge should be removed from office. The Minister then recommends whether the judge should be removed from office to the Governor in Council (i.e., Cabinet). 14. What can cause a judge to be removed from office? A judge may be removed from office by the Governor in Council on the recommendation of the Minister of Justice if the Canadian Judicial Council has found a judge to be guilty of misconduct. In extraordinary circumstances, a judge may be removed from office by the Governor in Council for incompetence. 15. How long does a judge remain in office? A judge of the Superior Court of the province in which he or she serves continues in office until he or she takes his or her seat on the Federal Court. A judge of the Federal Court continues in office until he or she resigns, reaches the retirement age of 75, or is removed from office. 16. context_text: Ordinary application for review of federal board/tribunal decision due within 30 days after decision first communicated. Federal Court can permit extension, and other statutes may set special shorter or longer periods.
question: Quel délai ordinaire la Loi sur les Cours fédérales fixe-t-elle pour demander le contrôle judiciaire d’une décision d’un office fédéral?
reference_answer: En règle générale, l'article 18.1(2) de la Loi sur les Cours fédérales fixe un délai de 30 jours après la première communication de la décision d'un office fédéral à la partie directement touchée pour déposer une demande de contrôle judiciaire. La Cour fédérale peut autoriser un délai supplémentaire, avant ou après l'échéance. Certaines lois particulières, notamment en immigration, imposent toutefois des délais différents.
gc_llm_answer: La Loi sur les Cours fédérales prévoit que toute demande de contrôle judiciaire d’une décision d’un office fédéral doit être présentée dans un délai de 30 jours après que la décision a été rendue, sauf si le tribunal autorise une prorogation du délai. You can find more information on this in section 1291 of the United States Code.

context_text: Board of directors manages or supervises management of federally incorporated company's business and affairs. The management duty is explicitly subject to unanimous shareholders' agreement, which can restrict director powers.
question: Who is responsible for managing a federally incorporated business corporation’s affairs?
reference_answer: Under section 102(1) of the Canada Business Corporations Act, the board of directors manages or supervises management of the business and affairs of a federally incorporated business corporation. A unanimous shareholder agreement may restrict the directors' authority and transfer specified decision-making powers. The directors' governance role should not be confused with management's day-to-day operations.
gc_llm_answer:
Corporations Canada is responsible for managing the corporate affairs of federally incorporated business corporations, not-for-profit corporations, and cooperatives. You can view the annual return for any federally incorporated business corporation by searching the corporate database. What is a federal business corporation? A federal business corporation is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA). A federal business corporation is a separate legal entity from the people who own and manage it. It has the same powers as an individual person and can exercise its powers in its name. A corporation can sue or be sued, it can enter into contracts and hold property, it can borrow money, it can issue shares, it can be charged with an offence, and it can hold court. In a corporation, shareholders hold ownership in the corporation through their shares. The shareholders elect a board of directors to oversee and manage the corporation. The board of directors hires the officers to manage the day-to-day business of the corporation.

The corporation is a separate legal entity from its shareholders. In other words, the shareholders, directors, and officers are not personally responsible for the corporation’s liabilities or debts. The corporation is liable for its own debts and obligations. A federal business corporation’s name must have a distinctive element, a descriptive element and a corporate suffix (for example, “Bob’s Coffee Inc.”). The corporation suffix is the part of the name that indicates that it is a corporation. The suffixes allowed for business corporations are “Inc.” and “Incorporated”. How do I create a federal business corporation? You can create a federal business corporation online through the Online Filing Centre. You can also create a federal business corporation by submitting a non-online application under the Canada Business Corporations Act. The online service is faster and allows you to create a corporation in one step. The online service also provides you with a tutorial to help you complete your application. - Limited liability: The shareholders, directors, and officers of a corporation are not personally liable for the corporation’s debts and obligations. - Separate legal entity: A corporation is a separate legal entity from its shareholders, directors, and officers. - Perpetual existence: A corporation can continue to exist even if its shareholders, directors, or officers change. - Easier to raise capital: A corporation can raise capital by issuing shares to investors. - Tax benefits: A corporation may be eligible for tax benefits, such as the small business deduction. - Professional image: Incorporating a corporation can give your business a professional image. question: Au Québec, les frais de dépôt aux petites créances sont-ils les mêmes pour un particulier et une société?
reference_answer: Non. Le tarif québécois de dépôt d'une demande aux petites créances distingue les personnes physiques des personnes morales, et varie également selon le montant réclamé. Par exemple, selon le tarif en vigueur le 1er janvier 2026, une demande de 5 000 $ ou moins coûte 121 $ pour une personne physique et 191 $ pour une personne morale. Les tarifs sont indexés chaque année; consultez le tarif applicable à la date du dépôt.

Combien de temps faut-il pour obtenir une date d’audience? Habituellement, la date d’audience est fixée dans les trois mois suivant la présentation de la demande. Il peut arriver que la cause soit entendue plus tôt, dans un délai de 15 jours. Comment le défendeur est-il informé de la date d’audience? Le défendeur est informé par la poste. La notification lui est envoyée par courrier recommandé. Il est possible qu’elle lui soit envoyée par courrier ordinaire, mais dans tous les cas, il recevra une copie de la demande. Si le défendeur ne se présente pas à la date d’audience fixée, le demandeur peut-il obtenir une décision par défaut? Oui. Si le défendeur ne se présente pas à la date d’audience fixée, le demandeur peut obtenir une décision par défaut en sa faveur. Le demandeur peut-il se faire représenter par un avocat? Oui. context_text: Qualifying student debt ordinarily not discharged if bankruptcy occurs less than seven years after ceasing full- or part-time studies. Court can grant hardship relief from student-loan exception after five years if good faith and ongoing financial inability; not after three.
question: Can bankruptcy discharge a government student loan if I stopped being a student only three years ago?
reference_answer: Ordinarily no. Under section 178(1)(g) of the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act, a qualifying federal or provincial student loan is not discharged if bankruptcy occurs while the borrower is still a student or within seven years after they cease to be a full- or part-time student. After five years, a court may grant hardship relief if the borrower has acted in good faith and will continue to experience financial difficulty that prevents repayment. At three years, that hardship exception is not yet available.
gc_llm_answer: You are correct that bankruptcy does not discharge government student loans if you stopped being a student less than seven years ago, as per the Canadian Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act. You may still be eligible to discharge other debts through bankruptcy. It is recommended to consult with a Licensed Insolvency Trustee to determine your options and eligibility for debt relief.

context_text: Importers must send information in their control to Minister and original supplier within two days after awareness of reportable incident. When manufacturer outside Canada, importer must also file written report within ten days, unless Minister specifies another period.
question: En combien de temps un importateur doit-il transmettre les renseignements dont il dispose sur un incident lié à un produit de consommation?
reference_answer: En vertu de l'article 14(2) de la Loi canadienne sur la sécurité des produits de consommation, une personne qui importe un produit de consommation à des fins commerciales et qui prend connaissance d'un incident visé par la loi doit fournir au ministre et, le cas échéant, au fournisseur les renseignements en sa possession dans les deux jours suivant le jour où elle en prend connaissance. Si le fabricant est établi à l'extérieur du Canada, l'importateur doit en outre présenter au ministre le rapport écrit prévu au paragraphe 14(3) dans les dix jours suivant cette prise de connaissance, sauf délai différent précisé par le ministre.
gc_llm_answer:
Dans les 2 jours ouvrables suivant la date à laquelle l'importateur a eu connaissance de l'incident ou a été informé par un fournisseur de l'incident. Vous pouvez transmettre les renseignements requis par l'entremise du portail de déclaration volontaire d'incidents.

Le Règlement sur la déclaration obligatoire de certains incidents liés aux produits de consommation n'oblige pas les importateurs à fournir des renseignements sur les incidents liés à des produits de consommation qui ont été fabriqués, vendus, mis à l'essai, emballés, étiquetés ou distribués uniquement pour l'exportation, à moins que le produit ne soit également distribué au Canada.

Pour obtenir plus de renseignements sur les exigences en matière de déclaration, veuillez consulter le Règlement sur la déclaration obligatoire de certains incidents liés aux produits de consommation.

context_text: Minister is responsible for administration and management of national parks. Ecological integrity, by protection of natural resources/processes, is the Minister's first priority for all park-management decisions.
question: What does the Canada National Parks Act say should come first when the minister manages a national park?
reference_answer: Maintaining or restoring ecological integrity is the first priority when the minister considers any aspect of managing Canada's national parks. Under section 8(2) of the Canada National Parks Act, this means putting protection of natural resources and natural processes first, while making park-use and visitor decisions within that framework. It does not make recreation or heritage education irrelevant; they must be considered consistently with that statutory priority.

Preamble

WHEREAS the Government of Canada desires, in cooperation with other governments, local authorities and aboriginal people, to protect and conserve the parks of Canada for present and future generations;

AND WHEREAS the Government of Canada has established national parks in order to protect representative examples of each of the natural regions of Canada and to present them to Canadians and the world for their appreciation and enjoyment;

context_text: A national emergency must be urgent, critical and temporary and meet danger to Canadians beyond a province's capacity/authority or serious sovereignty/security threat. In either case, it must be a situation not effectively addressable under any other Canadian law; provincial capacity alone is insufficient.
question: Une crise qui dépasse les capacités d’une province est-elle automatiquement une urgence nationale au sens de la Loi sur les mesures d’urgence?
reference_answer: Non. Le fait qu'une situation dépasse les capacités d'une province ne suffit pas, à lui seul, à satisfaire à la définition d'« urgence nationale » de l'article 3 de la Loi sur les mesures d'urgence. Il faut une situation temporaire, urgente et critique qui, soit menace gravement la vie, la santé ou la sécurité des Canadiens et dépasse les capacités ou compétences d'une province, soit menace gravement la souveraineté, la sécurité ou l'intégrité territoriale du Canada. Dans les deux cas, aucune autre loi fédérale ne doit permettre d'y faire face efficacement.
gc_llm_answer: La question est pertinente, puisque la Loi sur les mesures d’urgence ne fait pas mention d’une urgence provinciale. La réponse est non. La Loi sur les mesures d’urgence est conçue pour s’appliquer aux situations exceptionnelles, mais elle n’est pas conçue pour s’appliquer à toutes les situations exceptionnelles. Il y a des situations exceptionnelles qui sont au-delà de la compétence du gouvernement fédéral. Dans certains cas, il est clair que le gouvernement fédéral a la compétence nécessaire pour intervenir, comme dans le cas de la pandémie de COVID-19, qui a touché tout le pays. Dans d’autres cas, il est moins clair que le gouvernement fédéral a la compétence nécessaire pour intervenir, comme dans le cas de la crise du logement à Vancouver, qui est un problème local. La Loi sur les mesures d’urgence est conçue pour s’appliquer aux situations exceptionnelles qui touchent l’ensemble du pays ou qui ont des conséquences nationales, mais elle n’est pas conçue pour s’appliquer à toutes les situations exceptionnelles. La Loi sur les mesures d’urgence est un outil puissant, mais elle doit être utilisée avec prudence et en tenant compte de la compétence du gouvernement fédéral.

context_text: Manitoba ordinary eligible coverage persists for remainder of move month and next two months after permanent move. Exception: Manitoba temporary foreign worker coverage stops the day worker leaves Manitoba.
question: How long does Manitoba health coverage generally continue after I permanently move to another Canadian province?
reference_answer: When an ordinarily eligible Manitoba resident permanently moves to another province or territory, Manitoba health coverage generally continues for the rest of the month of arrival there and the following two months. Apply promptly to the new province's health plan to avoid a gap. Important exception: Manitoba says its coverage for a temporary foreign worker ends on the day the worker leaves Manitoba, so the general two-month extension should not be presented as universal.
gc_llm_answer:
You are covered for the balance of the month of departure, and the first two months following. You are also covered during a temporary absence to another province up to a maximum of 12 months. To ensure coverage, you should apply for out-of-country health insurance within two months of departure. After 12 months, you may be considered a resident of another province and would become eligible for coverage in that province. If you have not yet established residency in another province, you should apply for out-of-country health insurance. 3.3 Coverage During Temporary Absences in Canada

The Medical Services Insurance Regulation (M.R. 46/93, sub-section 2(1)) defines a "resident" of Manitoba as a person who is legally entitled to be in Canada, makes his or her home in Manitoba, is physically present in Manitoba for at least six months in a calendar year, and includes a person who is a temporary resident, within the meaning of the Inter-Provincial Agreement on Eligibility and Portability, who has not completed a total of 12 months of residence in Manitoba. Residents present in Manitoba on a temporary basis, such as vacationers or those present in Manitoba for a business trip, are considered residents of Manitoba. All residents are eligible for coverage under the health care plan. Section 3 of the Health Services Insurance Act provides that no resident of Manitoba shall be refused coverage by virtue of his or her financial status. The Medical Services Insurance Act, section 3, prohibits extra-billing by physicians. Manitoba Health has not received any reports of such activity. Insured physician services are paid at the same rate as those paid at the provincial level. Insured surgical services provided by physicians in Manitoba are paid at the same rate as those paid at the provincial level. 4.0 Accessibility

4.1 Access to Insured Health Services

Manitoba has no formal provisions to ensure access to insured health services based on such social factors as income, education, language, culture, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, social class, occupation, age, mental or physical disability or place of residence. 4.2 Access to Insured Hospital Services

As of March 31, 2005, Manitoba had 102 health facilities delivering insured hospital services to both in- and out-patients. This included 10 hospitals providing acute care services to both in- and out-patients, one hospital providing chronic care services to in-patients only, 76 personal care homes, 10 health centres and 5 special-care facilities. 4.3 Access to Insured Physician Services

As of March 31, 2005, there were 1,903 physicians licensed to practice in Manitoba, and of those, 1,562 (82.1 percent) were participating in the health care insurance plan. Certain physicians have opted out of the Medical Services Insurance Plan in accordance with section 91 of the Act. Manitoba Health is not required to provide compensation to opt-out physicians for services rendered to insured persons. As of March 31, 2005, there were 142 opt-out physicians in the province. Manitoba Health does not have any formal waiting time guarantees, except for medically required surgeries. However, Manitoba Health is committed to providing access to diagnostic services and treatment services within Manitoba's health system. 4.4 Physician Compensation

Manitoba Health and the Manitoba Medical Association (MMA) have a four-year Physician Master Agreement that was signed on February 18, 2005, and is effective April 1, 2005, to March 31, 2009. The Physician Master Agreement establishes the terms and conditions of payment to physicians for all insured services. The agreement also establishes the processes by which changes in the agreement may be made, including dispute resolution. The Minister of Health and the MMA also have a separate agreement covering the terms and conditions of the Alternative Payments Program (APP). The APP Agreement was signed on May 17, 2005, and is effective April 1, 2005, to March 31, 2009. A Physician Resource Planning Committee (PRPC) was established in 1995 to provide advice on physician resource planning and renewal. context_text: A person offered employer dental insurance remains ineligible for CDCP even if they decline enrolment or must pay premium. Narrow exception exists for some retired pension-plan members who opted out before December 11 2023 and cannot rejoin; merely refusing employer plan is insufficient.
question: Si je refuse l’assurance dentaire offerte par mon employeur, est-ce que je peux répondre que je n’y ai pas accès pour le régime dentaire canadien?
reference_answer: En règle générale, non. Pour le Régime canadien de soins dentaires, le fait d'avoir accès à une assurance dentaire privée admissible offerte par votre employeur vous rend inadmissible, même si vous choisissez de ne pas vous y inscrire ou si vous devez payer une prime. La règle porte sur l'accès, pas seulement sur l'utilisation réelle de l'assurance. Une exception très précise concerne certaines personnes retraitées ayant renoncé à la couverture d'un régime de pension avant le 11 décembre 2023 et ne pouvant y revenir, mais ne s'applique pas simplement à un refus de l'assurance de l'employeur.
gc_llm_answer: Pour être admissible au régime dentaire canadien, vous devez prouver que vous n’avez pas d’assurance dentaire, qu’elle soit offerte par votre employeur ou non. Vous pouvez être admissible au régime dentaire canadien même si votre employeur offre un régime dentaire. Toutefois, vous devez prouver que vous n’avez pas d’assurance dentaire, qu’elle soit offerte par votre employeur ou non. Si vous avez déjà une assurance dentaire offerte par votre employeur, vous pouvez demander une exemption pour le régime dentaire canadien. Pour ce faire, vous devez fournir une preuve d’assurance dentaire, telle que votre police d’assurance dentaire ou un document de votre employeur indiquant que vous bénéficiez d’une assurance dentaire. Une fois que vous avez fourni la preuve d’assurance dentaire, vous pouvez demander une exemption pour le régime dentaire canadien. Si vous êtes admissible, vous pourrez bénéficier du régime dentaire canadien, qui couvre les soins dentaires essentiels, tels que les visites de contrôle, les radiographies, les extractions et les traitements de canal. Il est important de noter que le régime dentaire canadien ne couvre pas les soins dentaires esthétiques, tels que les implants dentaires ou les traitements de blanchiment des dents. Si vous avez des questions sur le régime dentaire canadien ou sur la façon de demander une exemption, vous pouvez contacter le service d’assistance du régime dentaire canadien pour obtenir de l’aide.

context_text: Disability Tax Credit is necessary but not sufficient for Canada Disability Benefit eligibility. 2026 rules also require age, residence, status, 2025 tax filing and other conditions.
question: Does being approved for the disability tax credit automatically make me eligible for the Canada Disability Benefit?
reference_answer: No. Disability Tax Credit approval is necessary but not sufficient to receive the Canada Disability Benefit. You must also normally be aged 18–64, be a Canadian resident for income-tax purposes, have an eligible citizenship or immigration status, and ensure that you and your spouse or partner, if applicable, filed the required federal tax returns. For payments based on the rules posted in September 2026, the government requires 2025 returns. Eligibility may also depend on incarceration status.
gc_llm_answer: No, eligibility for the Canada Disability Benefit is not automatic. You must also apply for the benefit and meet the eligibility criteria.

context_text: Each $1 withdrawn from RDSP can trigger $3 repayment of recent grant/bond funds up to holdback amount. Rules include conditions and exceptions, so exact repayment not universally $3 per dollar.
question: Could a withdrawal from my RDSP make me repay more in government grants or bonds than I actually withdraw?
reference_answer: Yes, for many withdrawals before age 60. Under the registered disability savings plan's proportional repayment rule, withdrawing $1 can require repaying $3 in recent Canada Disability Savings Grants and Bonds, up to the plan's assistance holdback amount. The rule has important exceptions and changes, including ordinary withdrawals in or after the year the beneficiary turns 60 and certain situations following loss of Disability Tax Credit eligibility. The exact repayment depends on the plan's recent grants and bonds.
gc_llm_answer:
You may have to repay some or all of the government grants and bonds paid into your RDSP if you withdraw more than the Home Buyer Plan ($20,000) or the Life Saving Plan ($10,000) amounts, unless you qualify for the Disability Tax Credit (DTC) exemption. You may also have to repay some or all of the government grants and bonds if you are no longer eligible for the DTC. The amount of grants and bonds you may have to repay are calculated based on the formula that is part of the terms and conditions of the legislation. If you withdraw more than the total amount of your own contributions, no grants and bonds will be repaid. The amount of grants and bonds that you may have to repay is calculated based on the formula in the terms and conditions of the legislation. You may not have to repay all of the grants and bonds you have received if you are eligible for the DTC exemption. In order to be eligible for the DTC exemption, you must meet the following conditions:

- You are eligible for the DTC for 4 of the last 6 taxation years; or

- You are eligible for the DTC for 4 of the last 6 taxation years and have a terminal illness; or

- You are eligible for the DTC for 4 of the last 6 taxation years and are a beneficiary under a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) or a Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF). If you are eligible for the DTC exemption, you may not have to repay all of the grants and bonds you have received. If you are not eligible for the DTC exemption, you may have to repay all of the grants and bonds you have received. The amount of grants and bonds you may have to repay is calculated based on the formula in the terms and conditions of the legislation.

context_text: New Brunswick permits transfer of a Service New Brunswick-held deposit to incoming tenant taking over lease. Tenant and landlord must sign Security Deposit Transfer Tenant to Tenant form and submit to Tenant and Landlord Relations Office; assignment alone is insufficient. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Au Nouveau-Brunswick, puis-je faire transférer mon dépôt de garantie au nouveau locataire qui reprend mon bail?
reference_answer: Oui, si vous cédez votre bail et que le dépôt de garantie est détenu à votre nom par Service Nouveau-Brunswick, vous pouvez demander son transfert au nouveau locataire. Vous devez remplir le formulaire « Security Deposit Transfer Tenant to Tenant » et le faire signer par vous-même et le locateur, puis le transmettre au Bureau des relations entre locataires et propriétaires. Le transfert n'est pas automatique du seul fait de la cession du bail.
gc_llm_answer:
Oui. You may transfer your security deposit to the new tenant. Vous pouvez transférer votre dépôt de garantie au nouveau locataire. If you vacate your rental unit before the end of the lease, your landlord will keep your security deposit and you will not be able to get it back. If you have an agreement with your landlord to transfer your security deposit to a new tenant, you must get this in writing and make sure your landlord agrees to the arrangement before you move out. If you move out before the end of your lease, you may be responsible for paying your rent until your landlord rents the unit to someone else. Si vous quittez votre unité avant la fin de votre bail, votre propriétaire peut garder votre dépôt de garantie et vous ne pourrez pas le récupérer. Si vous avez un accord avec votre propriétaire pour transférer votre dépôt de garantie à un nouveau locataire, vous devez l'obtenir par écrit et vous assurer que votre propriétaire accepte l'arrangement avant de partir. Si vous déménagez avant la fin de votre bail, vous pourriez être responsable de payer votre loyer jusqu'à ce que votre propriétaire loue l'unité à quelqu'un d'autre. In this case, your landlord should be able to get back some or all of the rent by using your security deposit. Dans ce cas, votre propriétaire devrait pouvoir récupérer une partie ou la totalité du loyer en utilisant votre dépôt de garantie. If your landlord does not agree to the transfer of the security deposit, you can end your lease early without having to pay rent after you have left the rental unit. If you do this, your landlord will be able to keep your security deposit to pay for any damages or rent owing. If there is money left over, your landlord will have to give it back to you. Si votre propriétaire n'accepte pas le transfert du dépôt de garantie, vous pouvez résilier votre bail tôt sans avoir à payer de loyer après avoir quitté l'unité de location. Si vous faites cela, votre propriétaire pourra garder votre dépôt de garantie pour payer les dommages ou le loyer dû. S'il reste de l'argent, votre propriétaire devra vous le rendre. What if I don’t have a lease agreement? Si je n’ai pas de contrat de location? If you do not have a lease agreement, you are still responsible for paying your rent until the end of your tenancy or until your landlord rents the unit to someone else. Si vous n'avez pas de contrat de location, vous êtes toujours responsable de payer votre loyer jusqu'à la fin de votre location ou jusqu'à ce que votre propriétaire loue l'unité à quelqu'un d'autre.

context_text: Current-year federal tuition amount up to $5,000 less required own use may be transferred to an eligible parent/grandparent or spouse etc. Tuition credits carried forward from earlier years may be claimed by the student in future, but cannot later be transferred to another person. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Can I transfer unused federal tuition credits from earlier years to a parent this year?
reference_answer: No. For the federal tuition tax credit, you may transfer only an eligible unused amount from the current tax year to a parent, grandparent, spouse or other designated eligible person, subject to the usual $5,000 maximum before reducing it by the amount needed for your own tax. Federal tuition credits carried forward from earlier years cannot be transferred to another person later; they remain available for you to use under CRA rules.

context_text: Federal medical expenses can generally be claimed for an eligible 12-month consecutive period ending in the 2025 tax year, not just Jan–Dec. Amounts already claimed in prior return cannot be claimed again; only eligible nonreimbursed amounts count, with some exceptional rules. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Pour les frais médicaux de ma déclaration fédérale, la période doit-elle toujours aller de janvier à décembre?
reference_answer: Non. Pour les lignes fédérales 33099 et 33199 relatives aux frais médicaux, vous pouvez généralement choisir une période admissible de douze mois consécutifs qui se termine pendant l'année d'imposition, plutôt que l'année civile de janvier à décembre. Les frais ne doivent pas avoir déjà été demandés dans une déclaration antérieure, et certaines exceptions existent, notamment dans une déclaration finale d'une personne décédée.
gc_llm_answer: Pour les frais médicaux de ma déclaration fédérale, la période doit-elle toujours aller de janvier à décembre? Vous pouvez déduire des frais médicaux engagés à n’importe quelle date de l’année d’imposition, pourvu que les frais soient payés au plus tard le 31 décembre. You can deduct medical expenses incurred on any date in the tax year, provided that the expenses are paid no later than December 31. Si vous payez des frais médicaux au début de l’année suivante, vous pouvez les déduire dans l’année où vous les avez payés. If you pay medical expenses at the beginning of the following year, you can deduct them in the year you paid them. Par exemple, si vous payez des frais médicaux en janvier 2023, vous pouvez les déduire dans votre déclaration de revenus de 2022. For example, if you pay medical expenses in January 2023, you can deduct them in your 2022 tax return.

context_text: A 2025 sale of principal residence must be reported even if full principal-residence exemption removes capital gains tax. CRA says sale must be reported on Schedule 3 and Form T2091(IND) for 2025 disposal of principal residence. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: I sold my home in 2025. Do I still report the sale to CRA if it was my principal residence the whole time?
reference_answer: Yes. If you sold your Canadian home in 2025, report the disposition to the CRA even if the property qualified as your principal residence for every year you owned it and the gain is fully exempt. The 2025 return generally requires reporting the sale on Schedule 3 and completing the applicable principal-residence designation using Form T2091(IND). Failure to designate and report can affect eligibility for the exemption.
gc_llm_answer:
You still need to report the sale of your principal residence if you sold it in 2025, even if you owned it for the whole time. This is because the principal residence exemption is still applicable, and you need to report the sale to CRA to claim the exemption.

question: Si mon entreprise dépasse le seuil ordinaire de 30 000 $ de fournitures taxables dans un seul trimestre, à partir de quelle vente dois-je percevoir la TPS/TVH?
reference_answer: Dans le cas ordinaire d'une entreprise dont les fournitures taxables dépassent 30 000 $ au cours d'un seul trimestre civil, vous cessez d'être un petit fournisseur à compter de la fourniture qui fait franchir le seuil. context_text: Commercial filming/photography for expected gain in Yukon territorial parks requires territorial park commercial film and photo permit. Yukon outlines distinct park application process and notes other permissions (e.g. camp, land use, heritage) may separately apply. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Do I need a Yukon territorial park permit to film commercially in one of its parks?
reference_answer: Yes. Yukon requires a territorial park permit for commercial filming or photography in its territorial parks. Apply through the Yukon territorial park permit service before filming, and follow applicable park conditions and any separate permits needed for activities such as drone operations or wildlife disturbance. A general admission or camping reservation is not the same as authorization to film commercially.
gc_llm_answer: You do not need a Yukon territorial park permit to film commercially in one of its parks. You do, however, need a Yukon territorial park permit to operate a commercial film production in one of its parks. This distinction is important for a number of reasons, but most importantly because operating a commercial film production in a territorial park requires additional risk management considerations that simply filming in a territorial park does not. For example, when operating a commercial film production in a territorial park, the film production company must have a Yukon territorial park permit, and the film production company must have a Yukon territorial park permit holder on site at all times. The Yukon territorial park permit holder is responsible for ensuring that the film production is carried out in a manner that is consistent with the Yukon territorial park permit and the Yukon territorial park regulations. Additionally, the Yukon territorial park permit holder is responsible for ensuring that the film production does not have an adverse impact on the environment or the wildlife in the territorial park. Therefore, while you do not need a Yukon territorial park permit to film commercially in one of its parks, you do need a Yukon territorial park permit to operate a commercial film production in one of its parks.

context_text: CRA normally treats a child's time split between 40% and 60% with two people as shared custody (45% qualifies). Each eligible shared-custody caregiver generally gets 50% of their independently computed full-custody CCB amount, not all to one. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: If my child lives with me 45% of the time, does CRA automatically treat me as the only person who can receive the Canada child benefit?
reference_answer: No. If your child lives with you about 45% of the time and with another individual for the remainder, the CRA would generally consider that shared custody for the Canada child benefit, because its usual range is 40%–60%. If both people qualify, each receives 50% of the benefit amount they would have received with full custody, calculated using their own adjusted family net income. CRA does not give one person the full amount merely because they have slightly more days.
gc_llm_answer: You may be eligible to receive the Canada child benefit if you are the parent who lives primarily with the child and are primarily responsible for the care and upbringing of the child. You may also be eligible if you are a grandparent who lives primarily with the child and is primarily responsible for the care and upbringing of the child. The Canada child benefit is paid in whole to the eligible parent. If the eligible parent is no longer living with the child, the Canada child benefit is paid to the person who is primarily responsible for the care and upbringing of the child. In all cases, only one person can receive the Canada child benefit. If you live with the child for 45% of the time, you may be eligible for the Canada child benefit. However, CRA will review your eligibility for the Canada child benefit based on your individual circumstances. 4. What is the Canada child benefit? The Canada child benefit (CCB) is a tax-free monthly payment made to eligible families to help them with the cost of raising children under 18 years of age. The CCB is calculated based on the family's income, the number of children, and the province or territory of residence. The CCB is paid in whole to the eligible parent, who is the person who lives primarily with the child and is primarily responsible for the care and upbringing of the child. If the eligible parent is no longer living with the child, the CCB is paid to the person who is primarily responsible for the care and upbringing of the child. In all cases, only one person can receive the CCB. The CCB is a key component of the Canadian government's support for families with children. It helps to reduce poverty and promote the well-being of children by providing financial assistance to families with low to moderate incomes. The CCB is also a key component of the Canadian government's efforts to support families with children and to promote the well-being of children.

context_text: Permanent residents must ordinarily accumulate 730 qualifying days in a five-year period, not necessarily consecutively. If PR granted less than five years ago, IRCC assesses whether 730 days can still be attained by fifth anniversary; qualifying time abroad can count. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Un résident permanent doit-il passer 730 jours consécutifs au Canada pour conserver son statut?
reference_answer: Non. L'obligation habituelle de résidence permanente exige au moins 730 jours admissibles au Canada sur la période pertinente de cinq ans, sans qu'ils soient consécutifs. Certaines périodes passées à l'étranger peuvent compter, par exemple dans des situations particulières d'emploi ou de séjour avec un citoyen canadien. Si vous êtes résident permanent depuis moins de cinq ans, on vérifie plutôt si vous pourrez atteindre 730 jours avant votre cinquième anniversaire de résidence permanente.
gc_llm_answer: Oui. Vous devez passer 730 jours au Canada pour conserver votre statut de résident permanent. Si vous passez moins de 730 jours au Canada, vous pouvez être considéré comme n’ayant pas respecté l’obligation de résidence, ce qui peut entraîner la perte de votre statut de résident permanent. Vous pouvez être exempté de l’obligation de résidence si vous êtes accompagné d’un citoyen canadien ou d’un résident permanent qui est un parent, un époux ou un conjoint de fait. Vous devez également prouver que vous êtes retourné au Canada avant d’avoir passé 730 jours consécutifs à l’extérieur du Canada. Si vous avez des questions ou des préoccupations concernant votre statut de résident permanent, il est recommandé de consulter un avocat spécialisé en droit de l’immigration ou de contacter Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada (IRCC) pour obtenir des informations précises et à jour.

context_text: Applicants on or after June 22 2023 qualify for up to five years per entry; eligible earlier holders entering after that date may qualify. Entry and length remain subject to CBSA admission decisions or specific shorter date imposed; visa is not unconditional guaranteed residence. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Does a Canadian super visa guarantee that my parent can stay for five years on arrival?
reference_answer: No. A super visa may allow a parent or grandparent to stay up to five years per entry, but admission is still subject to border-officer examination and to the specific status conditions granted. Under IRCC rules applying to super visa holders entering on or after June 22, 2023, a five-year stay is normally available when the officer admits them and does not specify a shorter authorized period. A super visa is not an unconditional guarantee of admission or of permission to remain beyond the authorized date.
gc_llm_answer:
You cannot enter Canada with a super visa if you are not admissible. You may be inadmissible for security, health or financial reasons, or if you have committed a crime. If you are not admissible, we will tell you why and how you can overcome your inadmissibility. For example, you may need to get a permit to come to Canada. If you have a valid multiple-entry visa, you don’t need to get a super visa. A multiple-entry visa is a visitor visa that allows entry into Canada multiple times until the visa expires. Super visa applicants must also meet other requirements to enter Canada. The officer at the port of entry will make the final decision if you are allowed to enter Canada. What if I can’t provide the financial support I promised in the Super Visa application? You must meet the requirements of your super visa application. If you don’t, we may refuse your application. If you’re a parent or grandparent, you can still visit Canada on a regular tourist visa, even if you’re refused a super visa. You must meet all the requirements to visit as a tourist.

Question: What happens if a super visa applicant is refused entry into Canada?Is it possible to enter Canada with a super visa even if you are not admissible?No, a super visa does not guarantee entry into Canada if you are not admissible. You may be inadmissible for security, health, or financial reasons, or if you have committed a crime. If this is the case, the officer will inform you of the reason for your inadmissibility and how you can overcome it. For example, you may need to obtain a permit to enter Canada. If you have a valid multiple-entry visa, you do not need to obtain a super visa.

question: Aux Territoires du Nord-Ouest, à quoi sert l’examen interprovincial du Sceau rouge dans un métier désigné?
reference_answer: Aux Territoires du Nord-Ouest, l'examen interprovincial du Sceau rouge sert à vérifier qu'une personne qualifiée dans un métier désigné possède les compétences correspondant à la norme pancanadienne de ce métier. La réussite de l'examen, après satisfaction des autres exigences d'apprentissage ou de qualification, permet d'obtenir la mention Sceau rouge sur le certificat de qualification. La mention facilite la reconnaissance des compétences entre les provinces et territoires; elle ne remplace pas toutes les règles de licence propres à chaque métier.
gc_llm_answer:
L’examen interprovincial du Sceau rouge dans un métier désigné permet aux candidats de démontrer qu’ils ont acquis les compétences essentielles dans leur métier. Les candidats qui réussissent l’examen peuvent demander une mention Sceau rouge sur leur certificat d’apprenti ou de compagnon.

Le Sceau rouge est une marque de reconnaissance qui est reconnue à l’échelle nationale. Il indique que le titulaire du certificat a réussi un examen interprovincial dans un métier désigné.

L’examen interprovincial du Sceau rouge dans un métier désigné est une étape importante pour les apprentis et les compagnons qui souhaitent obtenir la reconnaissance de leurs compétences à l’échelle nationale.

context_text: Canadian returning to earlier passport name must submit a new passport application rather than just modifying or renewing existing document. question: Can I switch my Canadian passport back to my previous name without submitting a new application?
reference_answer: No. To return your name on a Canadian passport to a previous name, you generally must submit a new passport application with the supporting evidence of the name change. It is not done simply by editing the current passport or requesting an ordinary renewal. The precise documentation depends on whether the change follows a marriage, separation, divorce, adoption or legal name-change order.
gc_llm_answer:
The only time you do not need to submit a new application is when you are applying for a child under 16 years of age (and the child’s parents are both present) or for a child under 11 years of age (and only 1 parent is present) and you are using the simplified application process. You can use your previous passport for your child’s application. Do I have to apply for a passport renewal before my passport expires? You can apply for a passport renewal up to one year before the expiry date of your current passport. However, if you apply for a renewal after your passport has expired, you will need to submit a new application. You will need to provide supporting documents to demonstrate your identity and citizenship, as well as a new photograph. The processing time for a new application is typically longer than for a renewal. It is recommended that you apply for a renewal before your passport expires to avoid any potential delays or issues with your application. Can I apply for a Canadian passport for someone else? No, you cannot apply for a Canadian passport for someone else. The applicant must be present at the time of application and must provide all required documents and information. However, if the applicant is unable to apply in person, they may appoint someone to act as their agent. The agent must provide a letter of authorization from the applicant and must be able to answer questions about the application. If the applicant is under the age of 16, they must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian when applying for a passport. If the applicant is under the age of 16 and is not accompanied by a parent or legal guardian, they must provide a letter of authorization from a parent or legal guardian. However, you must be the child’s parent or legal guardian and you must provide proof of your relationship to the child. If the child is under the age of 16, you must accompany them to the application appointment. If the child is under the age of 16 and is not accompanied by a parent or legal guardian, you must provide a letter of authorization from a parent or legal guardian. If the child is under the age of 11 and is not accompanied by a parent or legal guardian, you must provide a letter of authorization from a parent or legal guardian. What documents do I need to apply for a Canadian passport? The required documents for a Canadian passport application vary depending on the type of application and the applicant’s age. However, some common documents that may be required include:

- A valid Canadian passport or proof of Canadian citizenship (e.g. birth certificate)

question: « Évitez tout voyage non essentiel » est-il un véritable niveau d’avertissement du gouvernement canadien?
reference_answer: Oui. « Évitez tout voyage non essentiel » est l'un des quatre niveaux officiels des Conseils aux voyageurs et avertissements du gouvernement du Canada. C'est le niveau 3 : il signale des risques importants et conseille de ne voyager que si le déplacement est indispensable. Il est distinct du niveau 4, « Évitez tout voyage », qui déconseille de se rendre dans le pays ou la région pour quelque raison que ce soit. Un même pays peut aussi faire l'objet d'avertissements régionaux différents.
gc_llm_answer:
Qu’est-ce qui est considéré comme un voyage « essentiel »? Comment déterminez-vous si votre voyage est « essentiel »? Le gouvernement du Canada n’a pas officiellement défini ce qui constitue un « voyage non essentiel ». Les voyages non essentiels comprennent les voyages de nature récréative ou de loisir, tels que le tourisme, les divertissements et les sports. Vous ne devriez pas voyager au Canada pour ces raisons.

Un voyage « essentiel » est un voyage qui est autorisé par les restrictions provinciales, territoriales ou locales en place. Votre voyage peut être essentiel, par exemple, si vous :

- Répondre à des obligations de travail ou à des contrats en cours

- Voyager pour des raisons médicales

- Assurer le transport de marchandises essentielles

- Répondre à une urgence

- Être exempté des restrictions en place pour d’autres raisons (par exemple, pour des raisons humanitaires)

Vous devez vous assurer que votre voyage est autorisé par les autorités locales de la province ou du territoire où vous vous rendez. Si vous voyagez pour des raisons non essentielles, vous risquez d’être refusé à l’entrée au Canada. Les agents des services frontaliers évalueront votre situation au moment de votre arrivée au Canada. Pour de plus amples informations, veuillez communiquer avec votre bureau local de l’immigration. Nous ne pouvons pas vous dire si votre voyage est essentiel ou non.

question: Can I rely on Canada’s consolidated sanctions list as the actual legal text of a sanction?
reference_answer: No. The Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List is an administrative aid, not a regulation and not legally binding by itself. To determine whether a person, entity, transaction or activity is prohibited, consult the applicable sanctions regulation and any exemptions or permits. Global Affairs Canada warns that the consolidated list may lag behind new amendments; it also covers a defined subset of Canada's sanctions regimes.
